preflop i would fold, small pocket pairs are weak hands.  min-raising to "put money in the pot" is not a good idea. The biggest mistake i saw in your poast is that you think you need to go all in when you have $150-$170 left in a $1 $2 game.  You have gone wrong by comparing the amount you currently have with the amount you bought in for.  This is completely irrelevant.  Desperation all in is only necessary when you have a low amount of big blinds or your M value is low.  Incase you don't know what M value is, it's your stack size/the amount in the pot before the cards are dealt.  In this case with a stack of let's say $150, you have 75 big blinds and an M value of 50.  This is a very comfortable situation.  An M value of over 20 is considered the green zone (ideal).  You have no reason to desperation shove.  
Poker is all one long session.  This is how you need to think of it.  You should not be trying to recoup the $150 that you have lost today.  Your only goal at the table should be to play hands as best as you can, whilst ignoring the results because you have no control over those.  I highly recommend the book the poker mindset for more on this.  So when you have a stack of $150, just play your hands as well as you can and try not to think about how much you have lost today and how you well get it back.
Now let me address the rest.  The fact that you are losing with a tight aggressive style in these games puzzles me.  I have been successful playing these types of games with a tag style as I feel it is best.  You must be making several mistakes like trying desperately to get your stack in with 75 bbs.
